title: Finite-type approximation of an affine nodal family
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] such that for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ [def-weil-geometric-point], the geometric fibre $X_\Omega$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre] is empty or equidimensional of dimension $1$ [def-weil-pure-dimension], and every point where $X_\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is not smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] has maximal-ideal-adic completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] isomorphic to $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $x\in X$ be a point at which $f$ is not smooth and set $s=f(x)$. There exist affine open neighbourhoods $X^\circ\subseteq X$ of $x$ and $S^\circ\subseteq S$ of $s$, with $f(X^\circ)\subseteq S^\circ$, schemes $X_0,S_0$ of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], a flat finitely presented morphism $f_0:X_0\to S_0$, and a Cartesian square $X^\circ\cong X_0\times_{S_0}S^\circ$ [def-pc-fibre-product] over a morphism $S^\circ\to S_0$. The morphism $f_0$ has the same geometric-fibre condition: every nonempty geometric fibre is pure of dimension $1$ and its completed local ring at every nonsmooth point is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. The image $x_0\in X_0$ of $x$ is nonsmooth for $f_0$. Here finitely presented means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated, as in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

source.place: Tag 0C5F (lemma-descend-nodal-family), combined with the absolute Noetherian approximation in the first paragraph of lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family; the geometric-fibre formulation is the equivalent nodal condition of lemma-nodal-family.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $S^\circ\ni s$ and then an affine open $X^\circ\ni x$ inside $f^{-1}(S^\circ)$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The restricted morphism $h:X^\circ\to S^\circ$ exists by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. Flatness and local finite presentation restrict by their local definitions [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The geometric fibres of $h$ are open subschemes of those of $f$, so they still have the stipulated completed local rings. They are empty or pure of dimension one: each component is a nonempty open of a component of the original fibre, whose dimension is unchanged by [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic]. Finally $x$ is nonsmooth for $h$, since smoothness of $h$ on a neighbourhood of $x$ would imply smoothness of $f$ there by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](b).

source.place: Tag 0CBY, first proof, first paragraph: affine localisation on X and S.

proof.text: Write $S^\circ=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lemma-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system-affine], it is the inverse limit of the spectra $S_i$ of finitely generated integer subalgebras of $A$, with affine transition morphisms. The affine morphism $h$ is of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). Apply [thm-pd-spreading-out](1) to get a stage $a$, a finitely presented $g_a:X_a\to S_a$, and $X^\circ\cong X_a\times_{S_a}S^\circ$ over $S^\circ$. For $i\ge a$ put $X_i=X_a\times_{S_a}S_i$ and $g_i:X_i\to S_i$. These maps remain finitely presented, and $X_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2)--(3). The system $(X_i)$ has limit $X^\circ$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit]. Passing to any directed tail retains this same limit, as is also included in that statement. Each $X_i$ is of finite type over $\mathbf Z$: finite-presentation chart algebras are finitely generated over their base chart algebras, and the union of two finite sets of generators generates their composite.

source.place: Tag 0CBY first proof first paragraph; Limits Tag 01ZM and Tag 01YZ for the models and their limit.

proof.text: For every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and every geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S^\circ$, the fibre $C=X^\circ_\Omega$ is a geometric fibre of $f$; if it is nonempty, all its closed points are smooth or nodes by the hypotheses retained in step 1. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-curve-lci-criterion], implication (1)$\Rightarrow$(2), over the algebraically closed field of this fibre. It makes $C$ a local complete intersection. The fibre is locally of finite type since local finite presentation is preserved by base change, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), and its algebra presentations remain finitely generated after dropping relations. Empty fibres are local complete intersections by the empty affine-cover convention. The generic descent result [lem-trf-complete-intersection-fibres-limit-descent], applied to $g_a$ over the given system, now gives $b\ge a$ such that every $g_i$ for $i\ge b$ is flat, locally finitely presented, and has local complete intersection geometric fibres over every algebraically closed field. Its qcqs hypotheses were checked in step 2.

source.place: Tag 0C5F, first proof sentence (Limits Tag 0C3L); the fibrewise interpretation of syntomicity from Tag 0C59 and Morphisms Tag 01UF.

proof.text: The ordinary nonempty fibres of $h$ are pure of dimension one as well. Here is the passage between ordinary and geometric purity that will also be used at finite stages. For a locally finite type scheme over a field, purity of dimension one is equivalent to local topological dimension one at every point: one direction is [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension] with the whole scheme as open; for the converse, at the generic point of each component take an affine neighbourhood and remove the finitely many other components through that chart, then [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic] identifies its local dimension with the dimension of this component. Finiteness of the components of these affine charts is [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]. The field-extension projection is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], since the map of one-point field spectra is surjective. Thus every ordinary-fibre point has a lift, and [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] identifies the two local dimensions. The same argument proves geometric purity from ordinary purity. Apply [lem-trf-pure-relative-dimension-finite-stage] to $g_b$ with $d=1$ to find $c\ge b$ such that every $g_i$ for $i\ge c$ has empty or pure-one-dimensional ordinary and geometric fibres.

source.place: Tag 0C5F dimension-one reduction; Limits Tag 0EY2 (existing pure-dimension descent); Morphisms Tag 02FY and Varieties lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic.

proof.text: Put $Z_c=\operatorname{Sing}(g_c)\hookrightarrow X_c$, the first-Fitting closed subscheme [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. Its formation commutes with every base change, without a nodality hypothesis: on an affine pair $R\to B$ and a base change $R\to R^\prime$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives $B^\prime=R^\prime\otimes_R B$, [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] identifies $\Omega_{B^\prime/R^\prime}=B^\prime\otimes_B\Omega_{B/R}$, and [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change](2) gives $\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{B^\prime/R^\prime})=\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega_{B/R})B^\prime$. The defining ideals therefore identify the closed subschemes and glue. In particular $Z_c\times_{S_c}S_i=\operatorname{Sing}(g_i)$ and $Z_c\times_{S_c}S^\circ=\operatorname{Sing}(h)$.

source.place: Tag 0C3I (lemma-base-change-and-fitting-ideal-omega), used in Tag 0C5F; More on Algebra Tag 07ZA(3).

proof.text: The schemes $S_c,X_c,Z_c$ are of finite type over $\mathbf Z$. For $Z_c$ this follows by taking a finite affine cover of $X_c$: the inverse image of each affine is its quotient by the defining ideal, and a quotient of a finitely generated algebra is generated by the images of the same generators. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] they are Noetherian, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Also $Z_c\to S_c$ is locally of finite type by the same quotient calculation. The limit morphism $\operatorname{Sing}(h)\to S^\circ$ is unramified by [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular], since $h$ has the required nodal geometric fibres. Step 5 identifies it with the base change of $Z_c\to S_c$. Apply [lem-trf-unramified-limit-descent] to this morphism of qcqs $S_c$-schemes. It gives $d\ge c$ such that $\operatorname{Sing}(g_d)\to S_d$ is unramified. Notice that this descent only requires local finite type for the singular morphism, so it does not assume that an arbitrary closed subscheme of a finitely presented scheme is finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 0C5F, last paragraph, using Limits Tag 0C4W (lemma-descend-unramified).

proof.text: We now recover the nodal condition on $g_d$. By steps 3--4 it is flat and finitely presented, and every geometric fibre $C$ is empty or pure of dimension one and a local complete intersection. For a nonempty such fibre over $\Omega$, step 5 identifies its first-Fitting singular scheme $Z_C$ with $\operatorname{Sing}(g_d)\times_{S_d}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. It is unramified by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open](1). Implication (2)$\Rightarrow$(1) of [lem-trf-nodal-curve-lci-criterion] therefore makes every closed point of $C$ smooth or a node. To cover every nonsmooth point, [lem-trf-dth-fitting-smooth-locus] with $d=1$ identifies that locus with $|Z_C|$, and [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-over-field-discrete] shows that every point of $Z_C$ is closed in $Z_C$. Since $Z_C$ is closed in $C$, each nonsmooth point is closed in $C$. It is thus a node; with $\Omega$ already algebraically closed, its defining completed-ring condition is exactly $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. The empty case is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 0C59, reverse implication, expanded using Tag 0C4E; Divisors Tag 0C3K and Morphisms Tag 02G7.

proof.text: Set $S_0=S_d$, $X_0=X_d$, and $f_0=g_d$. Step 2 gives finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and finite presentation; steps 3 and 7 give flatness and the required geometric-fibre condition. The two successive base changes identify $X^\circ\cong X_a\times_{S_a}S^\circ\cong X_d\times_{S_d}S^\circ$ by the fibre-product universal property. Let $x_0$ be the image of $x$. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-family-fitting-singular] to $f_0$: its singular subscheme pulls back to that of $h$, with underlying set the nonsmooth locus. Since $x$ is nonsmooth for $h$, its image lies in $\operatorname{Sing}(f_0)$ and $x_0$ is nonsmooth. All required data and the Cartesian square now have been constructed.

source.place: Tag 0CBY first proof first paragraph, including retention of the nonsmooth point under approximation.

tool_uses.why: Finiteness of the irreducible components of finite-type field-algebra charts is used in the local-dimension test for purity.
Constructs the affine finite-type integer inverse system; it is a generic approximation tool, not supplied by the trace-formula unit.
Only its object-descent clause is used for a finitely presented morphism over the affine limit, a generic scheme tool outside this unit.
Identifies the model base-change systems and their limits on directed tails, a generic limits tool.
Chooses affine opens inside prescribed neighbourhoods; a generic scheme-basis tool.
Constructs the restricted morphism from its image containment, a generic scheme factorisation tool.
Clause (b) ensures that nonsmoothness of x survives restriction of the target to an open.
Uses invariance of component dimension on nonempty opens for schemes locally of finite type over a field; no trace-formula node provides it.
Relates purity of a locally finite type field scheme to pointwise topological dimension for the field-extension comparison.
Uses the equality of local dimensions of corresponding fibre points under base change, a generic dimension tool.
Identifies affine differential modules before applying the existing Fitting-ideal base-change theorem, independent of nodality.
Base changes the finite-stage singular morphism to each geometric fibre.
Shows every singular geometric-fibre point is closed, so the existing closed-point nodal criterion covers every nonsmooth point.
